correctness.rationale: Solved the finite gambler-ruin recurrence to reconstruct the generating function D_h(z) of exact depth and duration; at z=1 depth has geometric exponential tail and H_max=(log n)/alpha+O_P(1). The analytic logarithm of u(e^s) gives conditional duration mean 2h/delta and variance 8pqh/delta^3. The forced initial loss step yields Catalan P(L=2m)=C_(m-1)p^m q^(m-1) and t^(-3/2)exp(-beta t) length tails. Chernoff concentration holds simultaneously across deterministic O(log n) thresholds, avoiding illicit independence at adaptive L_I; this gives O_P(1) rank relation and joint Slutsky limit. Independently checked exact gambler-ruin height laws for h=1..9 at p=3/4, and read source rational checker. No deterministic-calendar-time result.

originality.rationale: Wu (2026, arXiv:2610.41990) treats this same excursion/rank statistic, and its Theorem 1 and Example 2 *already establish* rank n^(1-rho+o_P(1)) and first-order duration ratio. Perfilev–Wachtel (2019) establish conditional CLT for a single large-height excursion, a prior component. Neither primary paper states the selected empirical rank sqrt(log n) Gaussian or the uniform threshold O_P(1) relation; these are the surviving advances, not the first-order exponent or single-excursion CLT.
residual_risks: Wu first-order result shares precisely the same model, so a future full general marked-extremes statement might subsume the Gaussian rank; no such implication appears in Wu primary theorem/proof. Oxford access was disconnected, but public arXiv text did permit direct inspection.

value.rationale: A natural second-order uncertainty law for a widely studied drawdown ranking statistic, including explicit correlation -1 and Catalan logarithmic rank correction; quantifies fluctuation beyond existing first-order exponent and is not a contrived finite slice.

final_claim: For fixed p in (1/2,1) and q=1-p, among n i.i.d. completed nonzero loss excursions of the +1/-1 biased walk, the selected deepest excursion duration L_I and descending rank R_n have joint sqrt(log n) Gaussian limit (Z,-beta Z), with Z variance 8pq/(delta^3 alpha), alpha=log(p/q), beta=-log(2 sqrt(pq)), delta=p-q. The sharper relation log R_n=log n-beta L_I-3/2 log L_I+O_P(1) holds.
limitations: Fixed p>1/2, independent completed *nonzero* excursions with forced initial loss; all durations even; ranking ties fixed; not deterministic physical time nor general increments; finite checks not proof.
